title: Rabbi Joey Soffer: Mesilat Yesharim class #11

chapters.title: Obstacles to Zrizut
chapters.about: Overly fearful behavior and its impact on performing mitzvot

chapters.title: Valid Caution vs. Nonsense Fear
chapters.about: Distinguishing between necessary self-preservation and yira shota

claims: "The lazy person's excuses" - The class discusses the lazy person's excuses as part of the section on 'yira shota' (nonsense fear), but it is not a distinct subject or part of the class structure as implied by the list.
"Zrizut after Zehirut" - While the teacher explains the relationship between the two, this is not a separate part of the class but rather a concluding explanation of the chapter.
summary: Rabbi Soffer continues his study of Perek Tet of Mesillat Yesharim, focusing on the character trait of zrizut and the obstacles that prevent it. He explains the difference between valid caution and 'yira shota' (nonsense fear), and then introduces the next trait, niki'ut, which involves purifying oneself from subtle desires that might lead one to justify a sin.
questions: What is the difference between a valid fear and nonsense fear?
Why does the Ramhal say that being lazy causes fear rather than the other way around?
How does zrizut follow zehirut in the process of spiritual growth?
What is the definition of niki'ut according to the Ramhal?
How does a person distinguish between a legitimate concern and an attempt to justify a sin?
